findings.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts:53 — One try/catch wraps the whole cancel loop, so the first SendGrid error stops every later cancel and skips the lazy deletes already queued (even for batches cancelled successfully), and cancelled-booking reminders still send.

packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts:57 — Rows already cancelled at SendGrid but not deleted get another cancel POST on every run: partial-failure leftovers, overlapping cron runs, or requestReschedule-flagged rows that handleNewBooking cancels right away. SendGrid rejects a duplicate batch status, so one such row can block the sweep until it ages out.

packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/emailReminderManager.ts:225 — Cancelling a booking now only sets cancelled=true (the old code cancelled at SendGrid right away), so a reminder due before the next cron run or inside SendGrid's roughly 10-minute cancel cutoff still sends, and the cron's past-due deleteMany (line 34) removes the flagged row without cancelling it.

packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/emailReminderManager.ts:213 — The immediateDelete branch cancels at SendGrid but never deletes or flags the DB row, so a reschedule leaves scheduled=true rows on the old booking that a later step edit or workflow delete cancels again.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:486 — Flagging reminders as cancelled is now fire-and-forget (the old DB deletes were awaited), here and in bookings.tsx:488, so the serverless response can return before the update lands and the unflagged reminder still sends.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/workflows.tsx:214 — Workflow and step deletion (also line 521) fire unawaited SendGrid cancels just before the cascade delete, so a swallowed failure (e.g. SendGrid's cap on active cancels during mass deletion) leaves no row to retry and the email for a deleted workflow still sends.

packages/prisma/schema.prisma:637 — The cancelled=true row is now the only record of a pending SendGrid batch, but booking onDelete Cascade removes it if the booking is deleted before the cron sweep, so the email sends.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:964 — This try/catch wraps a forEach of unawaited async calls, so it can never catch anything and gives false assurance that cancel failures are handled.

packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts:57 — A single SendGrid cancel failure throws out of the loop so remaining cancelled reminders are never cancelled (emails for cancelled bookings go out) and the lazily-built prisma deletes for already-cancelled batches never execute, so those batches get re-POSTed (and fail again) on every subsequent run.

packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts:48 — Cancellation is deferred to the cron's 1-hour window, so a booking cancelled/rescheduled shortly before its reminder (or picked up by a cron run only minutes before sendAt) is no longer cancelled in time and the reminder is still delivered, a regression from the previous immediate cancel.

packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/emailReminderManager.ts:213 — The immediateDelete path cancels the SendGrid batch but never deletes or flags the DB row (e.g. reschedule in handleNewBooking), leaving scheduled=true rows that later flows re-process and re-cancel an already-cancelled batch.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:488 — The reminder cancel/delete DB writes that were previously awaited via Promise.all are now fire-and-forget inside forEach, so the request can finish (serverless freeze) before reminders are marked cancelled and those reminders still get sent; same pattern in bookings.tsx:490 and workflows.tsx:378/576.

packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/emailReminderManager.ts:203 — Deciding from a stale in-memory referenceId=null to hard-delete the row races with the cron scheduling it concurrently, so the batch can be sent to SendGrid after its row is deleted and never gets cancelled.

packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/smsReminderManager.ts:180 — If twilio.cancelSMS throws (e.g. message already sent), the row delete is skipped, so SMS reminder rows for cancelled bookings/steps now linger where they used to be deleted unconditionally.

packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/emailReminderManager.ts:213 — immediateDelete path cancels the SendGrid batch but never deletes or flags the DB row, leaving stale scheduled=true, cancelled=null reminders (e.g. for the original booking on reschedule) that later code treats as live and may re-cancel.

packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts:56 — One try/catch wraps the whole cancel loop and the lazy delete promises only run at the end, so a single failed SendGrid cancel (e.g. a batch that was already cancelled) aborts the run, deletes no rows, and blocks every later cancellation until scheduledDate passes.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:486 — Reminder rows used to be deleted inside the awaited Promise.all, but the cancelled-flag/delete writes are now fire-and-forget async calls, so in serverless they can be dropped and cancelled bookings still get reminders.

packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/smsReminderManager.ts:178 — The row delete now shares a try block with twilio.cancelSMS, so a Twilio error (e.g. message already sent) leaves an orphan WorkflowReminder row that was previously always deleted.

packages/prisma/migrations/20230217230604_add_cancelled_to_workflow_reminder/migration.sql:2 — This migration dir already existed in base with an empty migration.sql and is being edited in place, so any environment that already applied the empty version gets a checksum mismatch and never adds the column.
packages/prisma/schema.prisma:644 — The new hourly cron query on (cancelled, scheduledDate) has no supporting index, which adds another full scan of WorkflowReminder on every run.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/workflows.tsx:213 — The same EMAIL/SMS if/else dispatch to deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder is copy-pasted in 7 call sites (workflows.tsx x4, bookings.tsx, handleCancelBooking.ts, handleNewBooking.ts); extract a single cancelWorkflowReminder(reminder, opts) helper.

packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/emailReminderManager.ts:197 — deleteScheduledEmailReminder is misnamed: without immediateDelete it only flags the row `cancelled: true` for the cron to process later, and with immediateDelete it cancels in SendGrid but never deletes the DB row.

packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/emailReminderManager.ts:200 — Optional boolean flag parameter `immediateDelete` selects between two unrelated behaviors (deferred DB flag vs. SendGrid cancel without row delete); callers pass a bare `true` that doesn't explain itself, so split it into two named functions.

packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/smsReminderManager.ts:177 — Email and SMS delete helpers now share the same signature but behave differently: SMS always hard-deletes the DB row, while email soft-flags it or leaves it in place, so reading any call site hides what actually happens to the row.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:968 — Reschedule in handleNewBooking passes immediateDelete=true, but the requestReschedule path in bookings.tsx:490 omits it, so the same lifecycle event behaves differently depending on the entry point with no comment explaining why.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:964 — The try/catch wraps a forEach of un-awaited async calls that already catch their own errors internally, so the catch block can never run and just adds misleading error handling.

packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts:57 — The SendGrid scheduled_sends cancel request is duplicated inline in the cron instead of reusing the one in emailReminderManager, so the cancel protocol now lives in two places.

packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts:54 — Uses the Prisma-internal generated type `Prisma.Prisma__WorkflowReminderClient<WorkflowReminder, never>`, leaking Prisma internals that break across Prisma upgrades; Promise<unknown>[] or PrismaPromise<WorkflowReminder>[] would do.

packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts:10 — Imports Prisma/WorkflowReminder as value imports from "@calcom/prisma/client" while the rest of the change imports from "@prisma/client", and both are used only as types.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:1 — Type-only imports (App, Credential, EventTypeCustomInput, Prisma) were merged from `import type` into a value import, which loses the type/value boundary and goes against the repo's consistent-type-imports style.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/workflows.tsx:2 — import type { Prisma, PrismaPromise }` was changed to a value import even though both are still used only as types (line 342), and `Prisma` on line 9 is missing its trailing comma (prettier drift).
packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/workflows.tsx:904 — The commented-out block had its indentation stripped, which adds diff noise to dead code and makes it harder to read; delete the block instead.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/workflows.tsx:574 — The `forEach(async (reminder) => ...)` callback no longer awaits anything, so the leftover `async` is dead and wrongly suggests the calls are sequenced.

packages/prisma/schema.prisma:644 — The new `cancelled Boolean?` is nullable with no default, making it tri-state (null/false/true) next to the non-null `scheduled Boolean`; `Boolean @default(false)` would be clearer.

packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/emailReminderManager.ts:206 — Delete logic now keys off `referenceId` being null instead of the `scheduled` column; `scheduled` is still written but no longer read for cancellation, which leaves two sources of truth for "was this sent to the provider".

packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts:57 — Cron awaits one SendGrid cancel request per cancelled reminder sequentially, so runtime grows linearly with reminders in the window and a mass cancellation can hit the serverless function timeout before the scheduling pass runs.

packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts:74 — Deletes are lazy PrismaPromises that only run after the whole SendGrid loop, and the whole loop sits in one try/catch, so one failed request or a timeout drops every delete and the next run re-sends the entire batch to SendGrid.

packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts:44 — New findMany on cancelled=true with scheduledDate has no take/limit and no index on (cancelled, scheduledDate), adding another full scan of WorkflowReminder on every cron run.

packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts:57 — A single failing SendGrid cancel throws out of the sequential loop, so every remaining cancelled reminder in the batch is skipped and its email is still sent.

packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts:74 — Prisma delete promises are lazy and only awaited after the loop, so when the loop throws, already-cancelled rows are never deleted and get re-POSTed on every cron run (a poison reminder that can block the batch until its scheduledDate passes).

packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts:77 — Batch cancellation failures are swallowed with console.log, with no per-reminder isolation, retry, or alerting, and the handler still returns 200.

packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/emailReminderManager.ts:233 — If the immediate SendGrid cancel or the cancelled-flag update fails, the error is only console.logged and nothing falls back to flag the row, so the reminder email goes out for a cancelled/rescheduled booking.

packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/emailReminderManager.ts:225 — Email cancellation is now deferred to the cron's last-hour window, so a missed or delayed cron run, or a cascade delete of the row (step/booking removal) before then, leaves the SendGrid batch uncancelled.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:964 — The try/catch wraps a synchronous forEach of unawaited async deletes, so it catches nothing and the cancellations run fire-and-forget during the reschedule.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:488 — Reminder cancellation/flagging is no longer part of the awaited Promise.all (the old DB deletes were), so the serverless function can return before reminders are marked cancelled.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx:490 — The `await Promise.all(remindersToDelete)` was removed and reminder cancellation is now fire-and-forget in requestReschedule, so the handler can finish before reminders are flagged or deleted.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/workflows.tsx:214 — Unawaited SMS/email cancellations race with the immediate workflow deleteMany cascade, so the SMS row delete can hit a missing record (P2025) that is only logged.
packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/smsReminderManager.ts:180 — If twilio.cancelSMS throws (e.g. already sent/cancelled), the DB row delete is skipped and the error is only console.logged.

packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts:56 — Deferred SendGrid cancellation loop aborts on first failed request (error swallowed), so remaining cancelled-booking reminders are never cancelled and emails with booking details are still delivered to recipients of cancelled/rescheduled bookings

packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/emailReminderManager.ts:197 — The new three-way state machine in deleteScheduledEmailReminder (null referenceId deletes the row, immediateDelete cancels in SendGrid but keeps the row, otherwise sets cancelled=true) ships with no tests for any branch.

packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts:44 — The new cron sweep for cancelled reminders (cancelled=true within the 1-hour window: SendGrid cancel, then row delete) has no tests for the window boundary, rows outside the window, or a null batch_id.

packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts:56 — No test covers a SendGrid failure partway through the sequential loop, where one throw stops all remaining cancellations and skips the queued deletes, so those reminders can still send.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:964 — The new reschedule path that cancels the original booking's reminders (EMAIL with immediateDelete=true, SMS delete) is untested, including that the immediateDelete email row is never deleted or flagged.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:486 — Cancellation dropped the scheduled/referenceId guard and the explicit prisma deleteMany, handing row cleanup to un-awaited helpers, and no test checks the final reminder rows (deleted vs cancelled=true) after a cancel.

packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/smsReminderManager.ts:177 — The changed deleteScheduledSMSReminder (skips Twilio when referenceId is null, now deletes the DB row, and a Twilio error skips the row delete because both share one try) has no tests.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx:488 — requestReschedule no longer awaits reminder cleanup (the helpers are fire-and-forget inside forEach), and no test checks that the reminders are flagged or removed before the mutation returns.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/workflows.tsx:574 — Edited steps now only flag old email reminders as cancelled=true while new ones get scheduled, and no test covers the old row sitting next to the new one or the cron sweep later cancelling it.

packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/emailReminderManager.ts:198 — The signatures of deleteScheduledEmailReminder and deleteScheduledSMSReminder changed from (referenceId) to (reminderId, referenceId, ...), but this repo snapshot has no tests and no other callers, so broken or stale callers and mocks elsewhere in the monorepo could not be checked.

goldens.comment: Asynchronous functions deleteScheduledEmailReminder and deleteScheduledSMSReminder are called without await inside forEach loops. This occurs during booking rescheduling/cancellation, and workflow/workflow step deletion/updates. Consequently, scheduled workflow reminders may not be reliably cancelled, potentially leaving them active.

When immediateDelete is true, the deleteScheduledEmailReminder function cancels the SendGrid email but fails to delete the corresponding WorkflowReminder record from the database. This creates orphaned database entries and is inconsistent with the immediateDelete: false path, which marks the record as cancelled. The SendGrid DELETE API call is also omitted in this path.

The 'cancelled' field is nullable, which can lead to existing records having null values instead of a default of false. This can cause incorrect behavior in the application when checking the cancellation status of reminders.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts:53 — One try/catch wraps the whole cancel loop, so the first SendGrid error stops every later cancel and skips the lazy deletes already queued (even for batches cancelled successfully), and cancelled-booking reminders still send.

adjudication.rationale: In `scheduleEmailReminders.ts`, the new cancellation block wraps the entire `for (const reminder of remindersToCancel)` loop and the final `await Promise.all(workflowRemindersToDelete)` in a single `try/catch`. If any `await client.request(...)` throws for one reminder, control jumps to `catch`, aborting cancellation for the remaining reminders and also skipping the final `Promise.all`, so previously queued `prisma.workflowReminder.delete(...)` operations are never awaited/executed. This can leave cancelled reminders in the DB and allow later reminders in the batch to remain uncancelled, matching the finding’s described behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts:57 — Rows already cancelled at SendGrid but not deleted get another cancel POST on every run: partial-failure leftovers, overlapping cron runs, or requestReschedule-flagged rows that handleNewBooking cancels right away. SendGrid rejects a duplicate batch status, so one such row can block the sweep until it ages out.

adjudication.rationale: In `scheduleEmailReminders.ts`, the new sweep selects `cancelled: true` reminders and, inside a single `try`, does `await client.request(... status: "cancel" ...)` per reminder and only *afterward* enqueues Prisma deletes and `await Promise.all(...)`. If any one `client.request` throws (whether due to duplicate cancel, transient API error, or overlapping runs), control jumps to the `catch` and the function skips deleting any of the reminders processed so far or still pending, leaving rows to be retried on subsequent runs. The finding’s specific claim that SendGrid rejects duplicate cancels isn’t verifiable from the diff, but the diff does show the retry/partial-failure behavior and lack of per-reminder error handling/idempotency safeguards.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/emailReminderManager.ts:225 — Cancelling a booking now only sets cancelled=true (the old code cancelled at SendGrid right away), so a reminder due before the next cron run or inside SendGrid's roughly 10-minute cancel cutoff still sends, and the cron's past-due deleteMany (line 34) removes the flagged row without cancelling it.

adjudication.rationale: In this diff, booking cancellation paths (e.g. `handleCancelBooking.ts` and `bookingsRouter` reschedule flow) now call `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId)` without `immediateDelete`. In `emailReminderManager.ts`, that code path does **not** cancel at SendGrid; it only marks the DB row `cancelled: true` (`prisma.workflowReminder.update(...)`). Actual SendGrid cancellation now happens later in `scheduleEmailReminders.ts` via a periodic job that finds `cancelled: true` reminders within the next hour and then POSTs `status: "cancel"` and deletes the row. Therefore, a reminder can still be sent by SendGrid between the booking cancellation and the next cron execution, which is a behavior regression/defect relative to immediate cancellation. The claim about a separate "past-due deleteMany" removing flagged rows without cancelling is not verifiable from the shown diff, but the delayed-cancellation window is directly grounded in the new logic.

In `emailReminderManager.deleteScheduledEmailReminder`, errors are caught and only logged, and when `immediateDelete` is true it does not mark `cancelled` in DB, so after the cascade delete there is no remaining row/state to retry cancellation; a scheduled SendGrid email for a deleted workflow/step can still send.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add `cancelled Boolean?` to `WorkflowReminder` and changes `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` to mark reminders as `cancelled` (instead of cancelling in SendGrid immediately) and a cron-like endpoint (`scheduleEmailReminders.ts`) later cancels/deletes those records. However, the finding’s key premise—“booking onDelete Cascade removes it if the booking is deleted”—is not shown or verifiable from this diff (the only visible `onDelete: Cascade` is on the `workflowStep` relation). The diff also does not show any booking-deletion path that would remove cancelled reminders before the sweep. So the claim that this will cause emails to send cannot be confirmed from the provided changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:964 — This try/catch wraps a forEach of unawaited async calls, so it can never catch anything and gives false assurance that cancel failures are handled.

packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts:57 — A single SendGrid cancel failure throws out of the loop so remaining cancelled reminders are never cancelled (emails for cancelled bookings go out) and the lazily-built prisma deletes for already-cancelled batches never execute, so those batches get re-POSTed (and fail again) on every subsequent run.

adjudication.rationale: In `scheduleEmailReminders.ts`, the cancellation/deletion logic is wrapped in a single `try { ... for (...) { await client.request(...) ; workflowRemindersToDelete.push(prisma.workflowReminder.delete(...)) } await Promise.all(workflowRemindersToDelete) } catch { ... }`. If `client.request` throws for any one reminder, control jumps to the `catch`, aborting the loop so later reminders are never cancelled. Additionally, the Prisma `delete(...)` calls are only accumulated and not awaited until after the loop; if an exception occurs before `Promise.all`, none of the queued deletes execute, so those same `cancelled: true` reminders will be retried on subsequent runs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts:48 — Cancellation is deferred to the cron's 1-hour window, so a booking cancelled/rescheduled shortly before its reminder (or picked up by a cron run only minutes before sendAt) is no longer cancelled in time and the reminder is still delivered, a regression from the previous immediate cancel.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes email reminder cancellation from immediate provider cancellation to a deferred DB flag in most call sites. `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminderId, referenceId, immediateDelete?)` now (when `referenceId` exists and `immediateDelete` is not set) only does `prisma.workflowReminder.update({ data: { cancelled: true } })` and does NOT call the provider cancel API. In booking-cancel/reschedule paths like `handleCancelBooking.ts` and `bookings.tsx`, it’s invoked without `immediateDelete`, so actual provider cancellation is postponed until `scheduleEmailReminders.ts` runs and finds `cancelled: true` reminders within the next hour. This introduces a real risk that a reminder close to send time can still be delivered before the cron/API job executes, which is a regression from the prior immediate cancel behavior shown in the removed code paths.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/emailReminderManager.ts:213 — The immediateDelete path cancels the SendGrid batch but never deletes or flags the DB row (e.g. reschedule in handleNewBooking), leaving scheduled=true rows that later flows re-process and re-cancel an already-cancelled batch.

adjudication.rationale: In `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminderId, referenceId, immediateDelete?)`, the `immediateDelete` branch cancels the SendGrid batch (`/v3/user/scheduled_sends` POST) and then `return`s without updating or deleting the `WorkflowReminder` row. Callers in this diff pass `true` (e.g. `handleNewBooking.ts` reschedule cleanup; `workflows.tsx` workflow/step deletion cleanup), and the previous explicit `prisma.workflowReminder.deleteMany(...)` cleanup was removed. As a result, reminders can remain in the DB (likely still `scheduled=true` and `cancelled` unset), so they won’t be picked up by the new DB-driven cancellation cleanup in `scheduleEmailReminders.ts` (which filters `cancelled: true`), leaving stale rows and potential repeated/incorrect processing later.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/emailReminderManager.ts:203 — Deciding from a stale in-memory referenceId=null to hard-delete the row races with the cron scheduling it concurrently, so the batch can be sent to SendGrid after its row is deleted and never gets cancelled.

adjudication.rationale: In emailReminderManager.deleteScheduledEmailReminder(), when the caller passes referenceId=null it immediately deletes the WorkflowReminder row (prisma.workflowReminder.delete). The function does not re-read the current DB state, so if the reminder is concurrently being scheduled by the cron (which will populate referenceId and create the SendGrid scheduled_send), this call can delete the row based on a stale in-memory null referenceId, leaving an already-created SendGrid batch with no DB record to later cancel (and scheduleEmailReminders.ts only cancels based on DB rows). That can lead to emails being sent after cancellation/reschedule with no cancellation path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/smsReminderManager.ts:180 — If twilio.cancelSMS throws (e.g. message already sent), the row delete is skipped, so SMS reminder rows for cancelled bookings/steps now linger where they used to be deleted unconditionally.

packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/emailReminderManager.ts:213 — immediateDelete path cancels the SendGrid batch but never deletes or flags the DB row, leaving stale scheduled=true, cancelled=null reminders (e.g. for the original booking on reschedule) that later code treats as live and may re-cancel.

packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts:56 — One try/catch wraps the whole cancel loop and the lazy delete promises only run at the end, so a single failed SendGrid cancel (e.g. a batch that was already cancelled) aborts the run, deletes no rows, and blocks every later cancellation until scheduledDate passes.

adjudication.rationale: In `scheduleEmailReminders.ts`, the new cancellation logic wraps the entire `for (const reminder of remindersToCancel)` loop in a single `try/catch` and performs DB deletes only after the loop via `await Promise.all(workflowRemindersToDelete)`. If any `await client.request(...)` throws mid-loop, control jumps to `catch`, skipping the remaining cancellations and also skipping all accumulated Prisma delete operations in `workflowRemindersToDelete` (none are awaited). This can leave cancelled reminders undeleted and prevent later reminders in the same run from being cancelled.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:486 — Reminder rows used to be deleted inside the awaited Promise.all, but the cancelled-flag/delete writes are now fire-and-forget async calls, so in serverless they can be dropped and cancelled bookings still get reminders.

adjudication.rationale: In handleCancelBooking.ts the code stopped collecting Prisma delete promises for workflow reminders and removed them from the awaited Promise.all. It now calls deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId) / deleteScheduledSMSReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId) inside nested forEach loops without awaiting them. Both deleteScheduled* functions are async and perform prisma.workflowReminder update/delete (and possibly external cancellation), so these writes are fire-and-forget and may not complete before the handler finishes (especially in serverless), leaving reminders not cancelled/deleted and potentially still sent.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/smsReminderManager.ts:178 — The row delete now shares a try block with twilio.cancelSMS, so a Twilio error (e.g. message already sent) leaves an orphan WorkflowReminder row that was previously always deleted.

adjudication.rationale: In smsReminderManager.ts, deleteScheduledSMSReminder now performs `twilio.cancelSMS(referenceId)` and then `prisma.workflowReminder.delete(...)` inside the same `try` block. If `twilio.cancelSMS` throws (e.g., cannot cancel because already sent), execution jumps to `catch` and the Prisma delete is skipped, leaving the WorkflowReminder row undeleted. Previously, the callers (e.g., handleCancelBooking.ts, bookings.tsx, workflows.tsx) separately deleted the reminder rows via Prisma regardless of cancel success; that deletion logic was removed in this diff, so the orphan-row risk is introduced by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/prisma/migrations/20230217230604_add_cancelled_to_workflow_reminder/migration.sql:2 — This migration dir already existed in base with an empty migration.sql and is being edited in place, so any environment that already applied the empty version gets a checksum mismatch and never adds the column.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `packages/prisma/migrations/20230217230604_add_cancelled_to_workflow_reminder/migration.sql` as `new file mode 100644` with an `index 000000..600081`, which indicates the file did not exist in the base revision and is being added, not edited in place. If an existing empty `migration.sql` were being modified, the diff would show a normal file change (not `new file mode`). Therefore the claimed checksum-mismatch scenario is not verifiable from this diff and is contradicted by it.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/prisma/schema.prisma:644 — The new hourly cron query on (cancelled, scheduledDate) has no supporting index, which adds another full scan of WorkflowReminder on every run.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new periodic query in `packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts` that does `prisma.workflowReminder.findMany({ where: { cancelled: true, scheduledDate: { lte: ... }}})`. The schema change adds `cancelled Boolean?` to `WorkflowReminder` and the migration only adds the column, with no `@@index`/`@index` shown in `schema.prisma` and no index creation in the migration. From what’s shown, this new filter (on `cancelled` plus a range on `scheduledDate`) has no supporting index added by the PR, making the performance concern actionable, but it’s not a correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/workflows.tsx:213 — The same EMAIL/SMS if/else dispatch to deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder is copy-pasted in 7 call sites (workflows.tsx x4, bookings.tsx, handleCancelBooking.ts, handleNewBooking.ts); extract a single cancelWorkflowReminder(reminder, opts) helper.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows repeated, near-identical dispatch logic `if (reminder.method === WorkflowMethods.EMAIL) ... else if ... SMS ...` across multiple files: handleCancelBooking.ts, handleNewBooking.ts, bookings.tsx, and several sites in workflows.tsx (e.g., around the deleted workflow cancellation, disabled event types, deleted steps, and edited steps). This is verifiable duplication introduced/expanded by the changes (new signatures `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId, ...)` / `deleteScheduledSMSReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId)`), and extracting a shared helper would reduce repetition and inconsistency risk, but it is not itself a functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/emailReminderManager.ts:197 — deleteScheduledEmailReminder is misnamed: without immediateDelete it only flags the row `cancelled: true` for the cron to process later, and with immediateDelete it cancels in SendGrid but never deletes the DB row.

adjudication.rationale: In `emailReminderManager.ts`, `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminderId, referenceId, immediateDelete?)` no longer reliably deletes the DB record: if `immediateDelete` is true it only sends the SendGrid cancel POST and then `return`s without deleting or even marking `cancelled=true`. Call sites in the diff (e.g. workflow deletion / step deletion) removed the prior `prisma.workflowReminder.deleteMany(...)` cleanup and now rely on this function, so scheduled reminders can be cancelled in SendGrid but left orphaned in the database and not picked up by the new cron cleanup (`scheduleEmailReminders.ts` only deletes rows where `cancelled: true`). The "misnamed" part is also accurate: the default path just flags `cancelled` rather than deleting.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/emailReminderManager.ts:200 — Optional boolean flag parameter `immediateDelete` selects between two unrelated behaviors (deferred DB flag vs. SendGrid cancel without row delete); callers pass a bare `true` that doesn't explain itself, so split it into two named functions.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminderId, referenceId, immediateDelete?)` uses a boolean flag to switch between distinct behaviors: if `immediateDelete` is truthy it issues a SendGrid cancel request and `return`s without updating the DB row; otherwise it updates the row to `{ cancelled: true }` (and if no `referenceId`, it deletes the row). Call sites pass a bare `true` (e.g. `workflows.tsx` for deleted workflows/steps), which is not self-documenting and makes the API easy to misuse. This is a concrete, diff-grounded API/design concern rather than a directly provable functional bug from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/smsReminderManager.ts:177 — Email and SMS delete helpers now share the same signature but behave differently: SMS always hard-deletes the DB row, while email soft-flags it or leaves it in place, so reading any call site hides what actually happens to the row.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `deleteScheduledSMSReminder(reminderId, referenceId)` always deletes the `workflowReminder` row (`prisma.workflowReminder.delete(...)`) after optionally cancelling Twilio, while `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminderId, referenceId, immediateDelete?)` may (a) hard-delete only when `referenceId` is null, (b) when `immediateDelete` is true it cancels the provider call and returns without deleting the DB row, or (c) otherwise just sets `cancelled: true` (soft flag) and keeps the row for later cleanup (e.g. `scheduleEmailReminders.ts` deletes flagged ones within the next hour). Since many call sites invoke both helpers similarly (same first two args), it is non-obvious from the call site whether the DB row is removed or merely flagged, making the reviewer’s concern about hidden behavior diff-grounded. This is a design/clarity/consistency issue rather than a directly verifiable functional defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:968 — Reschedule in handleNewBooking passes immediateDelete=true, but the requestReschedule path in bookings.tsx:490 omits it, so the same lifecycle event behaves differently depending on the entry point with no comment explaining why.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows two reschedule-related paths calling `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` with different semantics: in `handleNewBooking.ts` (around the new try/catch) it calls `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId, true)`, while in `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx` (around the reschedule logic) it calls `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId)` with no `immediateDelete`. Per `emailReminderManager.ts`, `immediateDelete=true` cancels via the external API and returns, whereas omitting it just marks the DB row `cancelled: true` for later cancellation. This is a real, diff-grounded inconsistency in lifecycle handling between entry points, but the diff alone doesn’t prove it’s an outright defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:964 — The try/catch wraps a forEach of un-awaited async calls that already catch their own errors internally, so the catch block can never run and just adds misleading error handling.

adjudication.rationale: In handleNewBooking.ts, the new try/catch wraps a synchronous `workflowReminders.forEach(...)` that invokes `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(...)` / `deleteScheduledSMSReminder(...)` without `await`. Since those functions are async, any rejection would occur asynchronously and would not be caught by this try/catch; additionally, both delete functions themselves have internal try/catch that logs and swallows errors, so they generally won’t throw anyway. That makes the outer catch block effectively misleading/unreachable based on the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts:57 — The SendGrid scheduled_sends cancel request is duplicated inline in the cron instead of reusing the one in emailReminderManager, so the cancel protocol now lives in two places.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts`, new logic loops `remindersToCancel` and directly performs `client.request({ url: "/v3/user/scheduled_sends", method: "POST", body: { batch_id: reminder.referenceId, status: "cancel" } })` and then deletes the reminder. The same SendGrid cancel protocol (POST to `/v3/user/scheduled_sends` with `{batch_id, status:"cancel"}`) also exists in `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` in `emailReminderManager.ts` when `immediateDelete` is true. So the cancel behavior is now implemented in two places rather than reusing the manager function. This is a maintainability/architecture issue, not a direct correctness defect shown by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts:54 — Uses the Prisma-internal generated type `Prisma.Prisma__WorkflowReminderClient<WorkflowReminder, never>`, leaking Prisma internals that break across Prisma upgrades; Promise<unknown>[] or PrismaPromise<WorkflowReminder>[] would do.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts` the diff adds `const workflowRemindersToDelete: Prisma.Prisma__WorkflowReminderClient<WorkflowReminder, never>[] = [];`, which is a Prisma-generated internal client type. This isn’t a runtime correctness bug in the diff itself, but it does unnecessarily couple the code to Prisma’s internal type names and can create upgrade fragility; a more stable type like `PrismaPromise<WorkflowReminder>[]` or `Promise<unknown>[]` would avoid that.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts:10 — Imports Prisma/WorkflowReminder as value imports from "@calcom/prisma/client" while the rest of the change imports from "@prisma/client", and both are used only as types.

adjudication.rationale: In scheduleEmailReminders.ts the diff does add `import { Prisma, WorkflowReminder } from "@calcom/prisma/client";` and they are only used in a type annotation (`Prisma.Prisma__WorkflowReminderClient<WorkflowReminder, never>[]`). However, this is not a verifiable defect from the diff: TypeScript tooling typically elides type-only usages at runtime even if not written as `import type`, and the diff doesn’t show any broken behavior caused by importing from `@calcom/prisma/client` vs `@prisma/client`. As stated, it reads as an import-style consistency/lint nit rather than a real bug or important issue grounded in the diff.

adjudication.rationale: In packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/workflows.tsx around the shown section (~923 in the diff), a large commented-out/dead-code block has its indentation removed (e.g., many lines lose leading spaces), which is indeed diff noise. adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/workflows.tsx:574 — The `forEach(async (reminder) => ...)` callback no longer awaits anything, so the leftover `async` is dead and wrongly suggests the calls are sequenced.

adjudication.rationale: In `workflows.tsx` the callback is indeed still written as `forEach(async (reminder) => { ... })` while no `await` remains inside after the diff. However, this is a stylistic/clarity nit (removing a now-unnecessary `async`) rather than a verifiable functional defect introduced by the change. The diff does not show any code that relies on the callback being sequenced, and `async` being present without `await` does not change runtime behavior here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/prisma/schema.prisma:644 — The new `cancelled Boolean?` is nullable with no default, making it tri-state (null/false/true) next to the non-null `scheduled Boolean`; `Boolean @default(false)` would be clearer.
matched_golden_ids: The 'cancelled' field is nullable, which can lead to existing records having null values instead of a default of false. This can cause incorrect behavior in the application when checking the cancellation status of reminders.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags that `cancelled` is nullable with no default, creating a tri-state (null/false/true) and recommends `@default(false)`. This matches the golden concern that nulls can exist (especially on existing records) instead of false and lead to incorrect cancellation checks.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/emailReminderManager.ts:206 — Delete logic now keys off `referenceId` being null instead of the `scheduled` column; `scheduled` is still written but no longer read for cancellation, which leaves two sources of truth for "was this sent to the provider".

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, cancellation paths were changed from checking `reminder.scheduled && reminder.referenceId` (e.g., removed in `handleCancelBooking.ts`, `bookings.tsx`, `workflows.tsx`) to calling `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId, ...)`, whose new logic in `emailReminderManager.ts` decides behavior based on whether `referenceId` is null and/or `immediateDelete` is set, and otherwise just marks `cancelled: true`. The `WorkflowReminder` model still has `scheduled Boolean` and code still queries unscheduled reminders via that flag (see `scheduleEmailReminders.ts` comment “find all unscheduled Email reminders”, and the pattern implies `scheduled` remains meaningful). This does create multiple state indicators (`scheduled`, `referenceId`, `cancelled`) and `scheduled` is no longer consulted for cancellation decisions, which is a concrete maintainability/consistency concern, though not a directly provable functional defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts:57 — Cron awaits one SendGrid cancel request per cancelled reminder sequentially, so runtime grows linearly with reminders in the window and a mass cancellation can hit the serverless function timeout before the scheduling pass runs.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts`, the new cancellation block does `for (const reminder of remindersToCancel) { await client.request(...) }`, which performs SendGrid cancel requests sequentially. Since this runs before the later "find all unscheduled Email reminders" scheduling logic, a large number of cancelled reminders within the 1-hour window could make the cron runtime scale linearly and risk a serverless timeout/delay, potentially preventing the scheduling pass from completing in time. This is a concrete scalability/performance issue visible in the diff, but not a guaranteed correctness defect in normal cases.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts:74 — Deletes are lazy PrismaPromises that only run after the whole SendGrid loop, and the whole loop sits in one try/catch, so one failed request or a timeout drops every delete and the next run re-sends the entire batch to SendGrid.

adjudication.rationale: In `scheduleEmailReminders.ts`, the new cancellation block wraps the entire `for (const reminder of remindersToCancel)` loop and the final `await Promise.all(workflowRemindersToDelete)` in a single `try/catch`. Inside the loop, each SendGrid cancel request is `await`ed, but the Prisma deletes are only queued as promises (`prisma.workflowReminder.delete(...)`) and not executed until the final `Promise.all`. If any `client.request(...)` throws mid-loop, control jumps to `catch` and the `Promise.all` is skipped, so none of the queued deletes run (including for reminders whose cancel request already succeeded earlier in the loop). Those rows remain `cancelled: true` and will be reprocessed on the next run, causing repeated cancellation attempts/cleanup failure. (The finding’s “re-sends the entire batch” wording is off—this code issues cancel requests, not sends—but the cleanup-skipping behavior is real.)

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts:44 — New findMany on cancelled=true with scheduledDate has no take/limit and no index on (cancelled, scheduledDate), adding another full scan of WorkflowReminder on every cron run.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new query in `packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts` that runs on each handler execution: `prisma.workflowReminder.findMany({ where: { cancelled: true, scheduledDate: { lte: ... }}})` with no `take`/pagination. That is a potentially unbounded read every cron run. Additionally, this PR introduces the new `cancelled` column in Prisma (`cancelled Boolean?`) but does not show any accompanying composite index (e.g., `@@index([cancelled, scheduledDate])`) being added; without it this query can degrade to a scan as the table grows. This is a performance/operational concern rather than a correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts:57 — A single failing SendGrid cancel throws out of the sequential loop, so every remaining cancelled reminder in the batch is skipped and its email is still sent.

adjudication.rationale: In packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts the new cancellation block wraps the entire `for (const reminder of remindersToCancel)` loop in a single `try { ... } catch { ... }`. If `await client.request(...)` throws for one reminder, control jumps to the `catch` and the loop stops, so remaining reminders are not cancelled/deleted. Those unprocessed reminders would keep their SendGrid scheduled send active, so their emails can still go out.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts:74 — Prisma delete promises are lazy and only awaited after the loop, so when the loop throws, already-cancelled rows are never deleted and get re-POSTed on every cron run (a poison reminder that can block the batch until its scheduledDate passes).

adjudication.rationale: In `scheduleEmailReminders.ts`, deletes are enqueued but not awaited until after the `for` loop (`workflowRemindersToDelete.push(prisma.workflowReminder.delete(...))` then `await Promise.all(...)`). Because the entire loop + `Promise.all` is wrapped in one `try`, if any `await client.request(...)` throws mid-loop, control jumps to `catch` and the queued Prisma delete operations are never awaited/executed, leaving those `cancelled: true` rows in the DB. Since the query selects `cancelled: true` rows every run, those undeleted reminders will be retried (re-POSTed) on subsequent cron runs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts:77 — Batch cancellation failures are swallowed with console.log, with no per-reminder isolation, retry, or alerting, and the handler still returns 200.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts` the newly added cancellation block wraps the entire batch in a single `try/catch` and on any failure only does `console.log(...)` (no rethrow/response handling). This means a single `client.request` error can prevent subsequent reminders from being cancelled/deleted, and the handler will continue executing and (by default) still return success, leaving cancelled/rescheduled reminders potentially still scheduled to send.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/emailReminderManager.ts:233 — If the immediate SendGrid cancel or the cancelled-flag update fails, the error is only console.logged and nothing falls back to flag the row, so the reminder email goes out for a cancelled/rescheduled booking.

adjudication.rationale: In `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` (emailReminderManager.ts), both the SendGrid cancel path (`immediateDelete` branch) and the DB update path are wrapped in a `try/catch` that only `console.log`s on failure. If the SendGrid cancel request fails, the function does not fall back to marking the reminder row `cancelled: true` (or deleting it), so the reminder remains eligible to be sent. This is especially problematic given the new retry/cleanup mechanism in `scheduleEmailReminders.ts` that relies on `cancelled: true` rows to cancel within the next hour; failures here prevent that mechanism from working.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/emailReminderManager.ts:225 — Email cancellation is now deferred to the cron's last-hour window, so a missed or delayed cron run, or a cascade delete of the row (step/booking removal) before then, leaves the SendGrid batch uncancelled.

adjudication.rationale: In emailReminderManager.deleteScheduledEmailReminder, the non-immediate path no longer cancels the SendGrid scheduled_send (it only sets WorkflowReminder.cancelled=true via prisma.workflowReminder.update). Actual SendGrid cancellation is moved to scheduleEmailReminders.ts, which only cancels rows with cancelled=true and scheduledDate <= now+1h. Therefore, if the cron/API route doesn’t run in that last-hour window, the SendGrid batch remains active and can still send for a cancelled/rescheduled booking. The “cascade delete of the row before then” part is less directly shown, but the deferral-to-cron risk is clearly introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:964 — The try/catch wraps a synchronous forEach of unawaited async deletes, so it catches nothing and the cancellations run fire-and-forget during the reschedule.

adjudication.rationale: In `handleNewBooking.ts` the new block under `if (originalRescheduledBooking?.uid)` uses `originalRescheduledBooking.workflowReminders.forEach(...)` to call `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(...)` / `deleteScheduledSMSReminder(...)`, but those functions are `async` (return Promises) and are not awaited or collected. As a result, cancellations run fire-and-forget while the handler continues, and the surrounding `try/catch` will not catch async rejections from those unawaited Promises (only synchronous throws inside the callback). This can lead to reminders not being cancelled in time and errors going unhandled/logged.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:488 — Reminder cancellation/flagging is no longer part of the awaited Promise.all (the old DB deletes were), so the serverless function can return before reminders are marked cancelled.

adjudication.rationale: In handleCancelBooking.ts the previous Prisma deleteMany operations were collected into `remindersToDelete` and awaited via `Promise.all(...)`. The new code calls `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId)` / `deleteScheduledSMSReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId)` inside nested `forEach` loops but does not `await` them and no longer includes any reminder-related promises in `prismaPromises`. Since these functions are `async` (and now perform DB `update`/`delete` to mark `cancelled` or remove the reminder), the handler can complete and return before those DB writes/remote cancellations finish.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx:490 — The `await Promise.all(remindersToDelete)` was removed and reminder cancellation is now fire-and-forget in requestReschedule, so the handler can finish before reminders are flagged or deleted.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx` the previous code collected Prisma delete promises (`remindersToDelete`) and `await Promise.all(remindersToDelete)`. The diff removes that await and now calls `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(...)` / `deleteScheduledSMSReminder(...)` inside `forEach` without `await`. Both functions are `async` (per the diff in `emailReminderManager.ts` and `smsReminderManager.ts`), so cancellations/deletes become fire-and-forget and the reschedule mutation can complete before the reminder updates/deletes run, which can lead to reminders not being reliably cancelled/deleted (especially in serverless/request-lifecycle scenarios).
